rows.q: Bette Davis warned party guests to fasten their seatbelts in All About Eve, but fans often misquote her by predicting a bumpy what, instead of a bumpy “night”?
rows.n: Davis’s raspy delivery was due to severe laryngitis; director Joseph L. Mankiewicz loved the sound and kept it.

rows.q: During production of The Deer Hunter, studio heads moved to fire a terminally ill John Cazale, until this acclaimed co-star and off-screen romantic partner threatened to walk off the film.
rows.n: Cazale completed all his scenes before dying of lung cancer months before the film’s premiere.

rows.q: As his cognitive modules are disconnected in 2001: A Space Odyssey, HAL 9000 slowly sings this Victorian tune, chosen because a real IBM computer sang it in 1961.
rows.n: Arthur C. Clarke attended the 1961 Bell Labs computer speech demonstration and suggested it to Kubrick.

rows.q: The hair-raising sword fight against seven living skeletons in 1963’s Jason and the Argonauts was brought to life frame by frame by this master of stop-motion.
rows.n: The skeleton sequence took Harryhausen four and a half months to animate for just minutes of film.

rows.q: Marni Nixon famously dubbed Natalie Wood in West Side Story, but five years earlier she provided the singing voice for Deborah Kerr in this Siam-set musical.
Director Howard Hawks and his chic wife Slim took credit for renaming Betty Joan Perske, giving this To Have and Have Not star what first name?
rows.n: Her mother’s maiden name was Bacal; Lauren added a second ‘l’ to ensure people pronounced it correctly.

rows.q: Fleeing a relentless super-posse in their hit 1969 western, Paul Newman and Robert Redford leave the frontier behind to rob banks in this South American nation.
rows.n: The real Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid were reportedly killed by Bolivian soldiers in 1908.

rows.q: Beloved for playing upright, noble characters in films like The Grapes of Wrath, this star shocked moviegoers by gunning down a child in Once Upon a Time in the West.
rows.n: Sergio Leone told Fonda to shave off his mustache and ditch his contacts so his blue eyes popped.

rows.q: Orson Welles ad-libbed a monologue in The Third Man mocking this neutral European country for only inventing the cuckoo clock—even though the clock is actually German.
rows.n: Graham Greene admitted Welles invented the speech on set, having read about Borgia-era Italy while traveling.

rows.q: Mel Brooks originally penned the role of Sheriff Bart in Blazing Saddles for this brilliant stand-up comedian and co-writer, whom studio executives refused to insure due to his reputation.
rows.n: Pryor stayed on as a credited screenwriter, crafting much of the dialogue for Cleavon Little and Mongo.

rows.q: Frank Sinatra coveted the role of high-roller Sky Masterson in 1955’s Guys and Dolls, but was furious when the singing lead went to this famously mumbling Method actor.
rows.n: Sinatra refused to speak to Brando between takes, referring to him only as ‘Mumbles.’

rows.q: Walter Neff and Phyllis Dietrichson plot murder in Billy Wilder’s Double Indemnity, picking this mode of transit because a policy clause pays out double for accidental death on it.
rows.n: James M. Cain’s novella was inspired by the real 1927 murder of Albert Snyder by Ruth Snyder and Judd Gray.

rows.q: Nominations for Best Makeup did not exist in 1968, but the Academy gave John Chambers an honorary award for designing the prosthetics in this landmark sci-fi film.
rows.n: Chambers used techniques he developed while making prosthetics for wounded military veterans.

rows.q: Liza Minnelli was named after an Ira Gershwin tune, but her parents famously met while her father directed her mother in this festive 1944 musical set in Missouri.
rows.n: Judy Garland and director Vincente Minnelli married in 1945, a year before Liza was born.

rows.q: Curt spends a frantic night in American Graffiti chasing a mysterious blonde in a Thunderbird, a role that launched this Three’s Company star.
rows.n: Somers had only one line in the film, silently mouthed through a car window: “I love you.”

rows.q: After starring as an alluring shopgirl in a smash 1927 silent film adapted from an Elinor Glyn novella, which Brooklyn actress was crowned the original “It Girl”?
rows.n: At her peak in 1929, she received more than 40,000 fan letters a month at the Paramount studios.

rows.q: Robert De Niro won Supporting Actor for The Godfather Part II speaking nearly entirely in this regional dialect, which he studied on location before filming.
rows.n: Only eight words spoken by his young Vito Corleone character in the film are in English.

rows.q: State censors in 1931 muted Colin Clive’s frantic rant in Frankenstein, drowning out his boast that animating the corpse revealed to him what it felt like to be this figure.
rows.n: Censors covered Clive’s blasphemous declaration with an artificial thunderclap, restored decades later.

rows.q: Fed up with uncompensated fourteen-hour makeup calls for Universal monster pictures, this horror icon served as an outspoken founding board member of the Screen Actors Guild in 1933.
rows.n: Karloff was SAG member number 9 and hosted clandestine union recruitment meetings at his Hollywood home.

rows.q: The first person to turn down an Oscar was screenwriter Dudley Nichols, who boycotted the 1936 ceremony because the Academy refused to recognize this guild he helped found.
rows.n: Nichols won for writing John Ford’s The Informer. He accepted the statuette three years later.

rows.q: Paul Schrader based Travis Bickle’s diary in Taxi Driver on the real-life journal of Arthur Bremer, who had attempted to assassinate this segregationist Alabama governor four years earlier.
rows.n: Bremer’s published book, An Assassin’s Diary, served as Schrader’s primary blueprint for Bickle’s isolation.

rows.q: German screen legend Marlene Dietrich created her famous first name as an eleven-year-old by squishing together her two birth names: Marie and this biblical name.
rows.n: Her breakout role as Lola Lola in 1930’s The Blue Angel launched her international career.

rows.q: Sergio Leone gave the American frontier an operatic, sun-baked makeover by filming his iconic Dollars Trilogy in the dry Tabernas Desert of this European nation.
Long before Terms of Endearment, Warren Beatty grew up sharing his birth surname with this Oscar-winning older sister, the star of The Apartment.
rows.n: She was born Shirley MacLean Beaty; their parents named her after child star Shirley Temple.

rows.q: Founded in 1934 by William Hinds, what British studio became synonymous with bloody gothic horror in the late 1950s after pairing Christopher Lee and Peter Cushing?
rows.n: Their breakthrough horror hit was 1957’s The Curse of Frankenstein, shot in vivid Eastmancolor.

rows.q: An eighteen-month-old Joseph Keaton took an unbroken tumble down a staircase, prompting this legendary escape artist to dub him ‘Buster.’
rows.n: Houdini traveled in the same vaudeville medicine-show circuits as Keaton’s parents.

rows.q: Twenty-four years after Hattie McDaniel won an Oscar for Gone with the Wind, which star took home Best Actor for Lilies of the Field?
rows.n: He became the first Black man to win an Academy Award, and the second Black acting winner overall.

rows.q: Prior to teaming with Humphrey Bogart in classic noirs, Peter Lorre starred in eight Fox mystery features as this polite Japanese secret agent created by John P. Marquand.
rows.n: Fox abruptly halted production on the popular series in 1939 due to rising geopolitical tensions with Japan.

rows.q: Decades before solving crimes in Cabot Cove, an 18-year-old Angela Lansbury earned an Oscar nomination in her film debut as an insolent housemaid in this 1944 thriller.
rows.n: Lansbury was working at a department store wrapping Christmas packages when she was cast by George Cukor.

rows.q: Actor David Niven titled his 1975 Hollywood memoir after a baffling instruction shouted on set by this Hungarian-born director of Casablanca and The Adventures of Robin Hood.
rows.n: During a cavalry scene, Curtiz meant riderless mounts when he bellowed for “empty horses.”

rows.q: Producer David O. Selznick feared the plot was absurd, but Alfred Hitchcock correctly chose this radioactive element as the smuggled contraband in his 1946 thriller Notorious.
rows.n: Hitchcock was placed under brief FBI surveillance after inquiring about uranium ore before Hiroshima.

rows.q: The first sequel ever nominated for Best Picture hit theaters in 1945, continuing the story of Bing Crosby’s Father O’Malley under this cheerful title.
rows.n: It was a sequel to Going My Way, which had won Best Picture the previous year.

rows.q: The famous opening line of Mean Streets—“You don’t make up for your sins in church”—is heard over a black screen, spoken not by lead actor Harvey Keitel, but by this uncredited filmmaker.
rows.n: Scorsese also stepped in front of the camera for a cameo as the hitman firing from a car at the climax.

rows.q: Born Joan de Beauvoir de Havilland, this Suspicion star took her stepfather’s surname to avoid professional conflict with her sister, who starred in Gone with the Wind.
rows.n: Fontaine beat Olivia for the 1941 Best Actress Oscar, intensifying a lifelong estrangement.

rows.q: Harold rejects his mother’s attempts to make him normal in Harold and Maude by using a blowtorch to transform this sleek British sports car into a hearse.
George C. Scott famously rejected his 1971 Best Actor award for Patton, having warned the Academy ahead of time that he found the competition a degrading ‘two-hour meat’ what?
rows.n: Producer Frank McCarthy accepted the trophy on Scott’s behalf, only to return it the next day.

rows.q: When Lauren Bacall asks, “You know how to whistle, don’t you, Steve?” she addresses Humphrey Bogart by the real-life personal nickname of this legendary director of the film.
rows.n: Bacall’s character was nicknamed “Slim,” which was the pet name of Hawks’s glamorous socialite wife.

rows.q: This five-letter studio won back-to-back Best Picture Oscars for Dances with Wolves and The Silence of the Lambs just before going broke.
rows.n: Founders chose the name because they believed the hunter’s constellation contained five primary stars like them.

rows.q: Before Margaret Mitchell settled on Scarlett O’Hara, the heroine of Gone with the Wind was given this floral first name in early drafts of the manuscript.
rows.n: Mitchell swapped in “Scarlett” just before publication; Tara was also originally named Fountenoy Hall.

rows.q: Before making his directorial debut with 1973’s Badlands, Terrence Malick taught philosophy at MIT and published an English translation of a 1929 book by this Being and Time philosopher.
rows.n: Malick translated The Essence of Reasons before leaving academia to join the American Film Institute.

rows.q: Steven Spielberg famously nicknamed the mechanical shark in Jaws “Bruce” after Bruce Ramer, who handled this professional duty for the young director throughout his Hollywood career.
rows.n: Ramer also represented Clint Eastwood and George Lucas throughout his decades in the film industry.

rows.q: Oliver Hardy is routinely misquoted as scolding Stan Laurel with “another fine mess.” Which four-letter synonym for pleasant did Hardy actually use on screen?
rows.n: The phrase “another fine mess” appeared only once across their films, as the title of a 1930 short.

rows.q: Lucille Fay LeSueur became Joan Crawford after a fan contest, and in 1929 she married this debonair actor, the namesake son of Hollywood’s greatest silent swashbuckler.
rows.n: Crawford’s father-in-law Douglas Fairbanks Sr. and stepmother-in-law Mary Pickford disapproved of the union.

rows.q: While location scouting in postwar Vienna for The Third Man, director Carol Reed was enchanted by musician Anton Karas playing this 36-string folk instrument in a wine tavern.
rows.n: Karas’s “The Harry Lime Theme,” performed entirely on zither, spent eleven weeks atop the U.S. pop charts in 1950.

rows.q: Lee Marvin won his sole Best Actor Oscar playing both a drunken, washed-up gunfighter and a vicious silver-nosed hitman in this 1965 musical comedy Western.
rows.n: Jane Fonda played the title character, a schoolteacher who turns outlaw to avenge her father’s murder.

rows.q: Charlton Heston angrily denied it, but this acerbic American author took credit for inserting a hidden romantic history between Judah and Messala in 1959’s Ben-Hur.
rows.n: Director William Wyler allegedly told Vidal to keep the subtext quiet from Heston.

rows.q: Before Martin Sheen took the lead in Apocalypse Now, Francis Ford Coppola fired this Mean Streets actor from the role of Captain Willard after just one week of shooting in the Philippines.
rows.n: Keitel was dismissed because Coppola felt his intense performance was too aggressive for a passive observer.

rows.q: King Kong famously concludes with the line “It was Beauty killed the Beast,” delivered by actor Robert Armstrong in the role of this obsessive theatrical showman.
rows.n: Director Merian C. Cooper modeled Denham on himself and co-piloted the plane that brought Kong down.

rows.q: In Dog Day Afternoon, when Sonny asks his nervous accomplice Sal which foreign country he wants to fly to, Sal causes a moment of bewildered silence by naming this landlocked U.S. state.
rows.n: John Cazale improvised the line on set, catching Al Pacino completely off guard.

rows.q: Following his Best Actor win for The Philadelphia Story, Jimmy Stewart mailed the gold statuette home to Pennsylvania, where his father kept it inside this retail business.
rows.n: J.M. Stewart Hardware kept Jimmy’s Oscar in the shop window for twenty-five years until his father passed away.

rows.q: In 1942, Hollywood star Hedy Lamarr was granted a patent for radio frequency hopping alongside this avant-garde American composer of Ballet Mécanique.
rows.n: Antheil’s experience coordinating sixteen synchronized player pianos helped inspire their 88-frequency mechanism.

rows.q: Because right-handed Gary Cooper couldn’t mimic Lou Gehrig’s southpaw swing in The Pride of the Yankees, director Sam Wood filmed him doing this immediately after hitting the ball.
rows.n: Cooper wore a mirror-image jersey reading “KROY WEN” so the technicians could flip the film negative.

rows.q: The Royal Theater in The Last Picture Show draws a tiny crowd for its final screening before closing forever, showing this 1948 Howard Hawks Western.
rows.n: Ben Johnson, who won an Oscar as Sam the Lion in Picture Show, had also appeared in Red River decades prior.

rows.q: To achieve the guttural, rasping voice of the demon possessing Linda Blair in The Exorcist, this veteran radio and screen actress chain-smoked cigarettes and swallowed raw eggs between takes.
rows.n: An Oscar winner for All the King’s Men, she had to fight Warner Bros. to receive on-screen credit.

rows.q: Before directing screwball masterworks like The Lady Eve, Preston Sturges made his early fortune by inventing an indelible, kiss-proof version of this cosmetic product.
rows.n: Sturges patented the smudge-proof formula while working at his mother’s cosmetics firm, Maison Desti.

rows.q: Hattie McDaniel became the first Black winner in 1940, but segregation barred her from sitting at the cast table at this legendary Los Angeles hotel’s Coconut Grove club.
rows.n: She and her escort were seated at an isolated two-person table at the rear wall of the ballroom.

rows.q: In Charlie Chaplin’s 1940 political satire The Great Dictator, Jack Oakie earned an Oscar nomination playing Benzino Napaloni, the pompous dictator of this fictional nation.
rows.n: Napaloni and Bacteria were thinly veiled satires of Benito Mussolini and Fascist Italy.

rows.q: After watching an early rough cut of Star Wars, this director friend stepped in to help George Lucas edit his convoluted, six-paragraph opening text into the famous three-paragraph crawl.
rows.n: Lucas also shared casting sessions with De Palma while the latter was casting his horror hit Carrie.

rows.q: Sophia Loren became the first star to win an acting Oscar for a foreign-language performance, starring in the 1961 Italian neorealist drama Two Women, directed by this man.
rows.n: Loren was so nervous about the 1962 broadcast that she stayed in Rome and slept through the ceremony.

rows.q: In the opening of All the President’s Men, the security guard who spots duct tape over a Watergate door latch is played by this real-life security guard who discovered the actual 1972 break-in.
rows.n: Wills was given only a brief cameo and struggled in poverty for much of his life following the scandal.

rows.q: The toxic high school in the 1988 dark comedy Heathers is named Westerburg High as an homage to Paul Westerberg, frontman of this Minneapolis alt-rock band.
In Pulp Fiction’s 1950s diner, Jack Rabbit Slim’s, Steve Buscemi cameos as an indifferent waiter dressed as this rockabilly legend.
rows.n: A cheeky inside joke from Tarantino, since Buscemi famously refused to tip waitresses in Reservoir Dogs.

rows.q: Jake Gyllenhaal nearly stepped in as Spider-Man after Tobey Maguire injured his back filming which 2003 true-life drama about an undersized racehorse?
rows.n: Maguire recovered just in time, but Gyllenhaal eventually entered the franchise in 2019 as Mysterio.

rows.q: James Cameron briefly considered which former NFL running back to play the Terminator, but decided audiences would find him too nice to be a killer?
rows.n: Simpson later played the accident-prone Detective Nordberg in the Naked Gun movies.

rows.q: Richard Linklater gave Waking Life and A Scanner Darkly their fluid, painterly look by having digital animators trace over live-action footage using this technique.
rows.n: Linklater used proprietary software called Rotoshop, created by computer scientist Bob Sabiston.

rows.q: Jackie Chan made blooper reels over the end credits his signature gimmick after appearing in this 1981 Burt Reynolds cross-country racing comedy.
rows.n: Director Hal Needham loved running outtakes, and Chan realized it proved to fans that his stunts were real.

rows.q: Eleven years after Kathryn Bigelow won Best Director for The Hurt Locker, which Beijing-born filmmaker took the trophy for Nomadland?
rows.n: She was only the second woman, and the first woman of color, to win the Academy Award for directing.

rows.q: Abandoned after devastating 1960s landslides, the Italian ghost town of Craco served as the backdrop for Judas’s hanging in what 2004 movie?
rows.n: Faulty infrastructure work accelerated the slope failure that forced Craco’s medieval center to evacuate.

rows.q: A jarring leap between rooftops in Mission: Impossible – Fallout left Tom Cruise with this broken bone, but he pulled himself up and finished the take used in the film.
rows.n: Production halted for seven weeks while Cruise rehabilitated his fractured right ankle.

rows.q: Stanley Kubrick shot Barry Lyndon under natural candlelight by tracking down rare f/0.7 lenses originally made by Carl Zeiss for this agency.
rows.n: NASA commissioned the ultra-wide-aperture lenses to photograph the dark side of the Moon.

rows.q: Crippled by a fear of flying in helicopters, this actor refused air shuttles to New Zealand mountain sets, choosing to hike for hours in full Boromir armor instead.
rows.n: Castmates flying above would spot Bean trudging through snowdrifts in his Gondorian costume.

rows.q: Low-ceilinged LesterCorp doesn’t occupy a full level of a Manhattan high-rise in Being John Malkovich, but rather this fractional floor.
rows.n: The cramped set required actors to walk hunched over through four-foot-high hallways.

rows.q: Sam Raimi’s yellow 1973 Delta 88 sedan has made a cameo in nearly all his films, from Evil Dead to Spider-Man. Which General Motors brand made it?
rows.n: Nicknamed “The Classic,” it was Raimi’s mother’s car before he started using it as a student filmmaker.

rows.q: Heath Ledger’s clown mask in the opening heist of The Dark Knight pays homage to one worn by this actor in a 1966 episode of the Batman television series.
rows.n: Romero wore the identical disguise in the season one episode ‘The Joker Is Wild.’

rows.q: Over nineteen years in Shawshank, Andy Dufresne concealed his wall tunnel behind posters of Rita Hayworth, Marilyn Monroe, and this 1960s star.
rows.n: The iconic poster shows Welch in a prehistoric doe-skin bikini from One Million Years B.C.

rows.q: Contractually, the lead in Die Hard had to be offered first to which 71-year-old crooner, who starred in the 1968 film adaptation of its prequel novel?
rows.n: Die Hard is based on Roderick Thorp’s novel Nothing Lasts Forever, a sequel to The Detective.

rows.q: To travel cross-country in Dumb and Dumber, Lloyd and Harry cruise inside an ‘84 Ford Econoline disguised as a sheepdog for this fictional grooming business.
rows.n: Jim Carrey had chipped his own front tooth years earlier and simply removed the cap for the role.

rows.q: Years before Danny Trejo hacked up bad guys in his own R-rated grindhouse movies, Robert Rodriguez introduced his character Machete as an inventor uncle in this family film.
rows.n: The character’s full name, Isador “Machete” Cortez, is identical across both movie series.

rows.q: Sofia Coppola’s dream-pop soundtracks often feature tracks by this French indie pop band, fronted by her husband Thomas Mars.
rows.n: The band won a Grammy in 2010 for their breakout fourth studio album, Wolfgang Amadeus Phoenix.

rows.q: That stormtrooper tricked by Rey into releasing her in Star Wars: The Force Awakens was secretly played by this British star, then filming Spectre on the very next soundstage.
rows.n: Craig’s character was designated FN-1824, and his voice was modulated in post-production.

rows.q: A pampered show dog with papers accompanies Walter Sobchak to the bowling alley in The Big Lebowski, representing this specific toy breed.
rows.n: Walter refuses to board it because, as he loudly explains to the alley, ‘It’s a show dog with papers!’

rows.q: Aiming to give his 1976 feature Heart of Glass an uncanny, trance-like rhythm, Werner Herzog famously put almost his entire cast under this psychological state before filming.
rows.n: Only one actor, playing the clairvoyant herdsman Hias, performed without being hypnotized.

rows.q: Nods to a galaxy far, far away abound in Indiana Jones, including the Shanghai club in Temple of Doom’s opening musical number, named after this Jedi Master.
rows.n: The scene opens with Kate Capshaw performing Cole Porter’s “Anything Goes” in Mandarin.

rows.q: Just weeks before her 2008 death, Majel Barrett completed recording her long-running franchise role as the voice of this shipboard system for the 2009 Star Trek reboot.
rows.n: Barrett voiced Federation computers across five television series and several feature films.

rows.q: “Anyone? Anyone?” In Ferris Bueller’s Day Off, Ben Stein’s droning teacher asks his silent class about this 1930 tariff act that worsened the Great Depression.
rows.n: Stein ad-libbed the economics lecture off the top of his head, having previously worked as a White House speechwriter.

rows.q: Hugh Jackman landed his breakout role as Wolverine in 2000 only after Dougray Scott was forced to drop out due to filming delays on this Tom Cruise spy sequel.
rows.n: Scott was trapped on set in Australia playing rogue IMF villain Sean Ambrose.

rows.q: In The Princess Bride, Westley survives a deadly battle of wits against Vizzini by having spent years building up an immunity to this fictional Australian poison.
rows.n: Author William Goldman invented the poison; real-world toxins rarely permit that kind of immunity.

rows.q: Glenn Close received an Oscar nomination for playing grandmother “Mamaw” Vance in this 2020 Ron Howard drama based on a best-selling political memoir.
rows.n: Close was nominated for both an Academy Award and a Golden Raspberry for the exact same performance.

rows.q: He finally won an Oscar in 2010 playing a washed-up country singer in Crazy Heart, nearly four decades after his breakout nomination in The Last Picture Show.
rows.n: His father Lloyd and brother Beau were also Emmy-nominated actors, making screen performance a family trade.

rows.q: Paul Thomas Anderson based Mark Wahlberg’s Dirk Diggler in Boogie Nights on this real-life 1970s adult film star, nicknamed ‘The King’.
rows.n: Holmes was also the notorious central figure tied to the 1981 Wonderland Avenue murders.

rows.q: In crafting the close-quarters fight style for 2002’s The Bourne Identity, Matt Damon underwent extensive training in Kali, a martial art from this archipelago.
rows.n: Kali heavily emphasizes weapon-disarming drills, which matched Bourne’s improvised fighting.

rows.q: Rather than building a studio set, The Truman Show filmed the idyllic town of Seahaven in this pastel, planned Florida beach community.
rows.n: Founded in 1981, Seaside is celebrated by architects as the pioneer of the New Urbanism movement.

rows.q: Actor Peter Cullen modeled the calm, authoritative voice of Optimus Prime on his brother Larry, who had returned from serving as an officer in this overseas conflict.
rows.n: Larry Cullen told Peter that real heroes do not scream and yell; they are quiet and strong.

rows.q: While wrecking the Flugelheim Museum to Prince tunes in the 1989 film Batman, the Joker slashes several masterworks but spares a gory canvas by this 20th-century British painter.
rows.n: The spared painting was Bacon’s 1954 work Figure with Meat, depicting a Pope flanked by raw carcasses.

rows.q: Harrison Ford filmed a cameo in E.T. that was ultimately cut from the movie, lecturing Elliott in the aftermath of the frog incident while playing this authority figure.
rows.n: Ford was dating screenwriter Melissa Mathison at the time, which led to his brief, deleted cameo.

rows.q: Director Emilio Estevez filmed his 2006 ensemble drama Bobby inside this historic Los Angeles hotel just months before wrecking balls flattened the site.
rows.n: The hotel famously hosted six Academy Awards ceremonies in its Cocoanut Grove nightclub.

rows.q: Adapting The Taming of the Shrew, 10 Things I Hate About You sent Heath Ledger courting Kat Stratford at a high school named for this Italian city.
rows.n: The film is an update of The Taming of the Shrew, which is set in the Italian city of Padua.

rows.q: Punxsutawney didn’t look picturesque enough on camera, so Groundhog Day filmed its endless winter loop in Woodstock, a small town in this Midwestern state.
rows.n: Woodstock still celebrates the movie every February with walking tours and a Groundhog Days festival.

rows.q: Maxed-out credit cards funded Kevin Smith’s indie Clerks, which was filmed overnight at this Leonardo, New Jersey convenience store where he worked by day.
rows.n: Smith explained the closed store shutters by having Dante claim someone jammed gum in the locks.

rows.q: Late-night donut runs in Wayne’s World take the duo to a pastry shop named in tribute to this real-life Chicago Blackhawks hockey star.
rows.n: Mikita spent 22 seasons with the Blackhawks and helped popularize the curved hockey stick blade.

rows.q: Martin Scorsese’s crime epic Casino chronicles the mobbed-up Tangiers, a fictional venue based directly on this real, starry Las Vegas hotel and casino.
rows.n: The Stardust was run by Frank Rosenthal, the real-life inspiration for De Niro’s Ace Rothstein.

rows.q: Kim Basinger took home an Oscar for L.A. Confidential playing a luxury escort surgically styled to resemble this peek-a-boo-banged 1940s noir icon.
rows.n: Lynn Bracken works for Fleur-de-Lis, an upscale call-girl ring with the motto ‘Whatever you desire.’

rows.q: John Woo first paired slow-motion gunplay with fluttering white doves in this 1989 Hong Kong classic starring Chow Yun-fat as an assassin with a conscience.
Guillermo del Toro frequently relies on this former contortionist and mime to inhabit his monsters, including the Faun in Pan’s Labyrinth and the Amphibian Man.
rows.n: Jones also endured four hours in makeup each day to play Commander Saru in Star Trek: Discovery.

rows.q: Playing Hans Gruber’s ruthless henchman Karl in Die Hard was a major pivot for Alexander Godunov, who had defected from the Soviet Union as a star in this art.
rows.n: Godunov was a principal dancer with the Bolshoi Ballet before defecting to the West in 1979.

rows.q: Before Zuul turns her apartment into a staging ground for Gozer, Dana Barrett makes her living in Ghostbusters playing this large string instrument in an orchestra.
rows.n: Sigourney Weaver took lessons so she could credibly mime playing alongside the New York Philharmonic.

rows.q: Beginning with Nausicaa of the Valley of the Wind in 1984, this composer has scored every one of Hayao Miyazaki’s feature films for Studio Ghibli.
rows.n: His professional stage name was chosen as a phonetic Japanese homage to American producer Quincy Jones.

rows.q: The cascading green code in The Matrix looks like alien cyber-text, but designer Simon Whiteley scanned the symbols from his wife’s Japanese books of these.
rows.n: Whiteley scanned katakana characters and numerals straight from his Japanese wife’s sushi cookbooks.

rows.q: In Marvel’s Black Panther, Daniel Kaluuya’s Border Tribe protects Wakanda while draped in patterned woolen blankets adapted from what real-life kingdom?
rows.n: The Basotho blanket became a national staple after King Moshoeshoe I received one from a British trader in 1860.

rows.q: That flame-throwing double-necked guitar in Mad Max: Fury Road was fully functional, with the burst of real fire controlled by pulling on this guitar accessory.
rows.n: Australian musician iOTA played the Doof Warrior while suspended from an eight-wheeled truck.

rows.q: Nicolas Winding Refn explained that the hyper-saturated, neon color schemes of Drive and The Neon Demon are a direct result of him living with this visual condition.
rows.n: Because he cannot perceive mid-tones, he requires extreme contrast and vivid primaries to see the image.

rows.q: While filming lab scenes for 2012’s The Avengers, Robert Downey Jr. hid real snacks on set, meaning this fresh fruit he casually offers Mark Ruffalo on camera was unscripted.
rows.n: The directors could not find his food stashes, so they just let him keep eating on camera.

rows.q: The Coen brothers edit almost all of their own films, but they submit their work to the Academy under this fictional British pseudonym.
rows.n: Jaynes has been nominated twice for Best Film Editing, for Fargo and No Country for Old Men.

rows.q: The atmospheric terraforming outpost overrun by xenomorphs on the moon LV-426 in Aliens bears this ironically hopeful, alliterative name.
rows.n: Only one of the settlement’s 158 colonists survived the initial siege: the young girl nicknamed Newt.

rows.q: After his grim tenure as 007, Timothy Dalton hammed it up as treacherous supermarket manager Simon Skinner in what 2007 Edgar Wright buddy-cop comedy?
rows.n: Dalton cheerfully leaned into his villainous image, delivering lines with a manic smile.

rows.q: Lionel Bart penned the romantic title tune for this 1963 thriller, with crooner Matt Monro performing the vocal heard over the closing credits.
Outside the United Kingdom, this historic transcontinental metropolis is the only city to host key location shoots for three different James Bond actors: Connery, Brosnan, and Craig.
rows.n: It hosted From Russia with Love, The World Is Not Enough, and Skyfall’s rooftop motorbike chase.

rows.q: The Parker Jotter grenade pen in GoldenEye is armed with a four-second fuse. Priming or disarming it requires clicking it this many times.
rows.n: Hacker Boris Grishenko nervously clicks pens while working, inadvertently arming the bomb in Trevelyan’s base.

rows.q: Carly Simon’s 1977 hit “Nobody Does It Better” was the franchise’s first theme not named after its film. Which Roger Moore movie featured it?
rows.n: The song still managed to work the phrase “the spy who loved me” into the lyrics.

rows.q: Famke Janssen’s sadistic assassin Xenia Onatopp dispenses with silenced pistols in GoldenEye, preferring to asphyxiate her targets between which body parts?
rows.n: Janssen bruised Pierce Brosnan’s ribs while shooting their wrestling fight in a sauna.

rows.q: Posing as an astrophysicist in Moonraker, Dr. Holly Goodhead is eventually revealed to be an undercover agent for which U.S. organization?
rows.n: Lois Chiles landed the role after sitting next to director Lewis Gilbert on an airplane.

rows.q: Hunting Bond’s future lover in the prologue of No Time to Die, vengeful chemist Lyutsifer Safin conceals his scarred face behind a mask from this Japanese theatre.
rows.n: The mask depicts a Ko-omote, a traditional Noh archetype portraying a serene young woman.

rows.q: Six years prior to barking Book ‘em, Danno on Hawaii Five-O, which actor became the first to portray CIA agent Felix Leiter on film in 1962?
rows.n: Producers dropped him from Goldfinger when he requested co-star billing and higher pay.

rows.q: Q outfits Bond with a fountain pen in Octopussy that melts through steel bars using this legendary acidic mixture of nitric and hydrochloric acid.
rows.n: Aqua regia is legendary in chemistry as one of the few reagents capable of dissolving noble metals like gold.

rows.q: Sean Bean was a top candidate to play Bond in GoldenEye before being cast as the villainous Alec Trevelyan. In the film’s prologue, Trevelyan was Bond’s MI6 partner with what 00 designation?
rows.n: 006’s Janus crime syndicate takes its name from the two-faced Roman god of transitions.

rows.q: Production designer Ken Adam built Blofeld’s hollow volcano lair on Pinewood’s backlot for over a million dollars, exceeding the entire production budget of this very first Bond film.
rows.n: The massive set featured a working monorail, a heliport, and a real steel retractable roof.

rows.q: Octopussy’s floating palace sanctuary was not a miniature or a studio tank, but an 18th-century royal pleasure palace floating on Lake Pichola in this Asian country.
rows.n: The white marble Taj Lake Palace in Udaipur was constructed by Maharana Jagat Singh II in 1746.

rows.q: The only woman James Bond ever lawfully married, Tracy di Vicenzo in On Her Majesty’s Secret Service, was portrayed by which late English actress?
rows.n: She was already famous worldwide for playing Emma Peel in the stylish 1960s series The Avengers.

rows.q: Before plunging his Lotus Esprit into the sea in The Spy Who Loved Me, Bond blinds an assassin’s pursuing car by spraying this wet construction material from behind his license plate.
rows.n: The spray blinded henchmen in a Ford Taunus, sending their car plunging off a cliff and into a farmhouse roof.

rows.q: Maurice Binder broke franchise tradition in 1981 by showing the singer on screen in the opening titles. Name this Scottish pop star of “For Your Eyes Only.”
rows.n: Binder chose to feature her because he found her extraordinarily photogenic.

rows.q: Known for fronting Soundgarden and Audioslave, which gritty rocker kicked off Daniel Craig’s run by singing “You Know My Name” in 2006?
rows.n: It was the first theme song since Octopussy not to feature the movie’s title in its lyrics.

rows.q: Mexico City never held an annual Day of the Dead street parade until 2016, when city officials launched one to capitalize on the opening chase scene from this 2015 007 film.
rows.n: Over 250,000 spectators attended the inaugural real parade, which copied the film’s skeleton floats.

rows.q: In The Living Daylights, Bond joins forces with an Oxford-educated guerrilla named Kamran Shah, who leads a band of fighters known by what collective term?
rows.n: Art Malik played Shah, who later helps Bond storm a Soviet airfield on horseback.

rows.q: Fronted by Scottish singer Shirley Manson, which 1990s alternative rock band delivered the dramatic title song for The World Is Not Enough?
rows.n: Composer David Arnold based the orchestral score around the band’s melody.

rows.q: While holding the dramatic, operatic final note of this 1965 title track, singer Tom Jones passed out cold in the recording booth. Name the movie.
rows.n: Jones replaced Shirley Bassey’s unused “Mr. Kiss Kiss Bang Bang” on short notice.

rows.q: Pierce Brosnan delivers one of the franchise’s groaniest puns to Denise Richards’ character, Dr. Christmas Jones, who improbably holds a doctorate in which field?
rows.n: Her expertise is needed to dismantle a stolen Soviet nuclear warhead in Kazakhstan.

rows.q: A migrating bullet lodged in the brain of terrorist Renard in The World Is Not Enough leaves him completely immune to this physical sensation.
rows.n: While the bullet makes Renard immune to fatigue, it is also slowly travelling through his brain and killing him.

rows.q: Which British singer won an Academy Award for co-writing and performing “Writing’s on the Wall,” the opening theme to 2015’s Spectre?
rows.n: Smith famously claimed to have written the lyrics in under thirty minutes.

rows.q: Jack White and Alicia Keys teamed up for the 2008 track “Another Way to Die,” marking the series’ first vocal duet. Which film opened with it?
rows.n: White also played drums on the track in addition to writing the lyrics.

rows.q: Pierce Brosnan’s Bond made an unforgettable 1995 debut by bungee-jumping 720 feet off the Contra Dam, a towering hydroelectric barrier located in this Alpine nation.
rows.n: Stuntman Wayne Michaels set a commercial world record for the highest jump from a fixed structure.

rows.q: Timothy Dalton’s second 007 outing was meant to be called Licence Revoked, until American test audiences confused it with losing the legal right to do this everyday activity.
rows.n: MGM panicked that Americans would think Bond was in trouble with the Department of Motor Vehicles.

rows.q: Pierce Brosnan was cast as Bond in 1986, but lost the role when 007 buzz prompted NBC to renew this slick private eye series co-starring Stephanie Zimbalist.
rows.n: The renewal backfired: ratings tanked, NBC cancelled it after just six episodes, and Brosnan waited nine years.

rows.q: Raoul Silva’s cyberterrorist headquarters in Skyfall is set on Hashima Island, a real Japanese ghost town abandoned after the closure of mines for this fuel.
rows.n: Known as Battleship Island, the site housed over 5,000 undersea miners for Mitsubishi until closing in 1974.

rows.q: Under the cover of an eco-charity in Quantum of Solace, Dominic Greene’s criminal enterprise conspires to monopolize this vital public utility across Bolivia.
rows.n: Greene dammed up the subterranean water table to sell the utility back to the state at inflated rates.

rows.q: Ian Fleming initially balked at casting Sean Connery, but Cubby Broccoli was persuaded after watching Connery sing and romance the village beauty in this 1959 Disney leprechaun fantasy.
rows.a: Darby O’Gill and the Little People
rows.n: Fleming quickly reversed his opinion after seeing Dr. No, adding Scottish heritage to Bond’s backstory.

rows.q: Seeking revenge for the murder of her marine archaeologist parents, Melina Havelock stalks villains in For Your Eyes Only armed with which archaic weapon?
rows.n: French actress Carole Bouquet could not film underwater scenes due to sinus issues.

rows.q: After his Lotus Esprit Turbo detonates its anti-theft bomb in For Your Eyes Only, Bond and Melina flee an ambush in this modest, air-cooled yellow French economy car from Citroën.
rows.n: Stunt driver Rémy Julienne installed a beefed-up flat-four engine from a Citroën GS to give the runabout speed.

rows.q: When Daniel Craig was unveiled as 007 in 2005, arriving via Royal Marines speedboat on the River Thames, the British tabloids mercilessly mocked him for wearing this piece of safety gear.
rows.n: Headlines dubbed him The Name’s Bland, James Bland and questioned whether he had the stomach for the role.

rows.q: Years before trading banter with Daniel Craig as Eve Moneypenny, Naomie Harris played which voodoo mystic in two Pirates of the Caribbean sequels?
rows.n: The character is later revealed to be the bound sea goddess Calypso.

rows.q: Oddjob actor Harold Sakata claimed an Olympic silver medal in weightlifting sixteen years before Goldfinger, representing not Japan but this home country.
rows.n: Born in Hawaii, Sakata took silver in the light-heavyweight division at the 1948 London Games.

rows.q: Barbara Bach’s Soviet agent Anya Amasova shares equal billing with 007 in The Spy Who Loved Me under which three-letter KGB codename?
rows.n: She vows to kill Bond after their mission when she learns he shot her lover in Austria.

rows.q: To stop stunt cars from sliding across Matera’s slick cobblestones in No Time to Die, the production crew sprayed thousands of gallons of this fizzy beverage on the streets.
rows.n: The evaporating soda left a sticky sugar film that provided tire grip without staining the stone.

rows.q: Louisiana Sheriff J.W. Pepper, played by Clifton James, was so popular in Live and Let Die that producers had him bump into Bond on vacation in which Asian nation?
The villainous vendetta driving Alec Trevelyan in GoldenEye stems from the WWII British handover of this equestrian ethnic group to Soviet forces at Lienz.
rows.n: Trevelyan’s parents survived the 1945 Betrayal of the Cossacks only to commit suicide from survivor’s guilt.

rows.q: Years before Dr. No hit cinemas, Barry Nelson starred in a 1954 CBS TV adaptation of Casino Royale, where his 007 was reimagined as an American with what first name?
rows.n: His agency was also changed from MI6 to the Combined Intelligence Agency.

rows.q: Barbara Broccoli was convinced Daniel Craig had the grit to play 007 after watching him star as an unnamed, sharp-suited cocaine distributor in what 2004 Matthew Vaughn crime thriller?
rows.n: Vaughn later directed the Kingsman franchise, which heavily spoofed and homaged the Bond series.

rows.q: When delivering the remote-controlled BMW 750iL at Hamburg Airport in Tomorrow Never Dies, Q poses as an employee of this real-world car-rental giant, sporting their red jacket.
rows.n: Q reminds Bond that any scratches or damage to the high-tech vehicle will completely void the rental agreement.

rows.q: Honor Blackman was cast as Pussy Galore in Goldfinger largely because producers admired her judo skills as Cathy Gale on which British TV series?
rows.n: Her judo training on the show convinced director Guy Hamilton she could handle Connery.

rows.q: Gemma Arterton’s Bolivian consular agent in Quantum of Solace suffers an oil-drenched death honoring Goldfinger. What is her fruit-flavored first name?
rows.n: Her full name, Strawberry Fields, is a Beatles pun only revealed in the end credits.

rows.q: During the chaotic 1967 spoof Casino Royale, Peter Sellers refused to share the set with this larger-than-life Le Chiffre actor, forcing crew members to film their card game scenes separately.
rows.n: Sellers reportedly stormed off when Princess Margaret visited the set and greeted Welles before him.

rows.q: Sean Connery almost lost the role to this actor, who turned down 007 over moral objections. Five years later, he created and starred in the surreal cult classic The Prisoner.
rows.n: He famously played Number Six, trapped in a mysterious coastal village while insisting he was not a number.

rows.q: In Goldfinger’s laser table scene, Sean Connery was genuinely terrified because the glowing red line was actually being cut through the metal from below by this handheld tool.
The daring stuntman who skipped across live crocodiles in Live and Let Die owned the Jamaican reptile farm; producers honored him by naming this villainous character after him.
rows.n: Stuntman Ross Kananga took five takes and suffered severe bite wounds to his legs during the shoot.

rows.q: Aboard the Orient Express in From Russia with Love, assassin Donald Grant blows his English cover when he pairs a glass of red Chianti with this delicate flatfish.
rows.n: Bond famously reflects on Grant’s error later: ‘Red wine with fish. That should have told me something.’

rows.q: Producers first asked a 21-year-old Timothy Dalton to replace Connery in 1968, right after he made his film debut as King Philip II of France in this Katharine Hepburn period drama.
rows.n: Peter O’Toole starred as King Henry II; Dalton felt he was too young to step into Connery’s shoes.

rows.q: Famous for his theatrical laugh as Baron Samedi in Live and Let Die, polymath Geoffrey Holder won two 1975 Tony Awards for his work on this hit musical.
rows.n: Holder was the first Black director in Broadway history to win the Tony for Best Direction of a Musical.

rows.q: To emphasize his maritime obsession in The Spy Who Loved Me, villain Karl Stromberg was scripted with this subtle physical abnormality on his hands.
rows.n: Jurgens wore small latex webs between his fingers, though the feature is only fleetingly shown on camera.

rows.q: Alongside a magnetic pulse to unzip dresses, Q Branch fitted the Rolex in Live and Let Die with this small power tool to cut ropes.
rows.n: Production designer Syd Cain built the prop by filing teeth into a real Rolex bezel and mounting a tiny motor.

rows.q: Between 1968 and 1981, this comedian held court in the center square of Hollywood Squares, delivering hundreds of saucy zingers to host Peter Marshall.
rows.n: He once answered the question ‘What makes the wind blow?’ with ‘Two beans and a glass of milk.’

rows.q: When the British murder mystery Broadchurch was remade for Fox as Gracepoint, this Scottish actor was cast as the lead detective in both versions.
rows.n: He adopted an American accent for Gracepoint, where his character was renamed Emmett Carver.

rows.q: Setting the template for 90s Thursday comedies, Wings followed two pilot brothers running a one-plane airline based on this Massachusetts island.
rows.n: Sandpiper Air flew out of Tom Nevers Field, named after an actual headland on the island’s south coast.

rows.q: Before Richard Mulligan starred on Empty Nest, the spin-off was introduced on The Golden Girls as an unsold concept starring this EGOT-winning West Side Story actress.
rows.n: The concept was heavily retooled, dropping Moreno’s character and turning Harry Weston into a widowed pediatrician.

rows.q: The US version of The Office relocated Dunder Mifflin to Scranton, while Ricky Gervais’s original UK series doomed its paper salesmen to this Berkshire town.
rows.n: Poet John Betjeman famously mocked the town in 1937: ‘Come, friendly bombs, and fall on Slough.’

rows.q: Marc Summers spent years covered in green slime on Nickelodeon’s Double Dare, despite privately living with this condition that made messes agonizing.
Ken Jennings’ historic 74-game winning streak on Jeopardy! ended in 2004 when he incorrectly named FedEx instead of this tax-prep firm.
rows.n: The winning contestant, Nancy Zerg, lost her very next game.

rows.q: In a 1994 Seinfeld episode, Jerry and Elaine head to a bakery for a chocolate version of this Eastern European pastry, only to get stuck with cinnamon.
rows.n: Elaine famously declared cinnamon the ‘lesser’ version of the braided pastry.

rows.q: Upon commandeering a Martian gunship called the Tachi, the crew in The Expanse christened it with this name borrowed from Don Quixote’s trusty steed.
rows.n: In the novels, Holden names the ship because Rocinante was a workhorse that became a noble steed.

rows.q: David Milch originally pitched HBO a drama about cops in ancient Rome, but swapped out centurions for gunslingers when HBO greenlit this competing sword-and-sandal series.
rows.n: Rome and Deadwood ended up airing concurrently on HBO in the mid-2000s.

rows.q: When NBC imported The Weakest Link in 2001, this sarcastic British journalist kept her hosting job, greeting American contestants in all-black attire and a trademark wink.
rows.n: Her frosty persona was inspired by her years as an abrasive London tabloid editor.

rows.q: Showtime adapted its counterterrorism thriller Homeland from Prisoners of War, an acclaimed 2010 drama originally produced in this Middle Eastern country.
rows.n: Gideon Raff created the original Hebrew series, titled Hatufim, before co-developing Homeland.

rows.q: While Ian Hunter wrote the anthem ‘Cleveland Rocks,’ this 1990s alternative trio behind ‘Lump’ recorded the version used to open The Drew Carey Show.
rows.a: The Presidents of the United States of America
rows.n: The Seattle trio’s upbeat cover replaced The Vogues’ ‘Five O’Clock World’ as the theme in season three.

rows.q: Created by Shawn Ryan, what gritty FX police drama followed the corrupt Strike Team led by Detective Vic Mackey through the fictional streets of Farmington?
rows.n: Michael Chiklis won both an Emmy and a Golden Globe for playing Mackey during the show’s first season.

rows.q: Tommy Shelby enters British politics in Peaky Blinders to infiltrate a fascist movement led by this real-life baronet and founder of the British Union of Fascists.
rows.n: Actor Sam Claflin portrayed Mosley’s chilling rise in British politics in the 1930s.

rows.q: Set around Manchester’s Canal Street, the original 1999 version of Queer as Folk was penned by this Welsh creator who later revived Doctor Who.
rows.n: Showtime adapted the show in 2000, moving the setting from Canal Street to Pittsburgh.

rows.q: Benson DuBois left the chaotic Tate household of Soap to manage the home of James Gatling, an absent-minded politician holding this executive state office.
rows.n: Over seven seasons on Benson, Robert Guillaume’s character rose from head of household to lieutenant governor.

rows.q: Robert Redford’s 1994 film Quiz Show dramatized the scandal that brought down this 1950s NBC quiz program, where contestants played in soundproof booths.
rows.n: Producers fed answers to contestant Charles Van Doren to help him defeat Herb Stempel.

rows.q: Geralt of Rivia shows a startling lack of variety when naming his animal companions, bestowing what humble, fishy moniker on every horse he rides?
rows.n: In the original Polish books, the horse’s name is Plotka, referring to the common European freshwater roach.

rows.q: Besides hosting the chaotic 1970s talent parody The Gong Show, this TV producer wrote the pop hit “Palisades Park” and claimed to be a CIA hitman.
rows.n: His 1984 memoir Confessions of a Dangerous Mind was adapted into a movie by George Clooney.

rows.q: Helen Mirren became a global star playing DCI Jane Tennison on this ITV police procedural, later remade on NBC with Maria Bello in the lead role.
rows.n: Created by Lynda La Plante, the UK original won multiple Primetime Emmy Awards for Miniseries.

rows.q: In a 1998 SNL dinner-table sketch, an enraged Will Ferrell demands respect from his family by screaming that he drives what midsize sedan?
rows.n: Ferrell’s character Gene screams that he can do a hundred pushups in twenty minutes and that people are afraid of him.

rows.q: David Spade spent seven seasons playing smarmy assistant Dennis Finch at a fictional fashion magazine on this Must-See TV workplace sitcom.
rows.n: Created by Steven Levitan, the show paired Spade with George Segal, Wendie Malick, and Laura San Giacomo.

rows.q: Coined in 1978 to sneak past broadcast censors, what four-letter substitute for a common profanity became a hallmark of the rebooted Battlestar Galactica?
rows.n: Original series creator Glen A. Larson spelled it with a ‘c’ before the 2004 reboot dropped the letter.

rows.q: Stefan Karl Stefansson spent a decade playing the scheming villain Robbie Rotten on this acrobatic Icelandic children’s show that became an unlikely global hit.
rows.n: Created by aerobics champion Magnus Scheving, the show was recorded in a dedicated English-language studio in Iceland.

rows.q: Voiced by series co-creator Deborah Pratt, what is the name of the ego-driven, parallel hybrid supercomputer advising Sam Beckett on Quantum Leap?
rows.n: Pratt also provided the uncredited opening voiceover narration for the series.

rows.q: Long before commanding the USS Voyager as Kathryn Janeway, this actress played Peter Falk’s oft-mentioned but never-seen wife in the 1979 spin-off Mrs. Columbo.
rows.n: Falk disapproved of the show, and producers hastily renamed the lead and divorced her from Columbo in season two.

rows.q: On Will & Grace, Karen Walker carried on a venomous rivalry with socialite Beverley Leslie, played by this diminutive Southern character actor.
rows.n: Jordan won an Emmy in 2006 for playing Beverley, a role originally intended for Joan Collins.

rows.q: Before Jack Tripper shared an apartment with two women in Santa Monica, Robin Tripp did the same in London on this 1970s ITV sitcom.
rows.n: Richard O’Sullivan starred as Robin Tripp, who was enrolled in culinary school like Jack.

rows.q: In season four of The Sopranos, a grieving Bobby Baccalieri refuses to defrost the final frozen casserole his late wife Karen made: this dish.
rows.n: Janice Soprano eventually maneuvers Bobby into eating it, marking a key turning point in his mourning.

rows.q: Daria Morgendorffer escaped the idiot slackers of Highland on Beavis and Butt-Head when her cynical family relocated to this fictional, pastel-soaked suburb.
rows.n: MTV executives specifically commissioned the spin-off to bring in more female viewers to their animated block.

rows.q: Hawkins teenagers spent the summer of 1985 eating sundaes and dodging Soviet operatives beneath this neon-drenched fictional shopping mall.
rows.n: The mall scenes were filmed inside the partially abandoned Gwinnett Place Mall outside Atlanta, Georgia.

rows.q: Bruce Willis appeared on Friends without taking home a paycheck after losing a bet to Matthew Perry over the box office fate of this 2000 comedy.
rows.n: Willis donated his guest fees to charity after the mob comedy debuted at number one in the U.S.

rows.q: Before building Waystar Royco in New York, Succession patriarch Logan Roy grew up in poverty in this Scottish coastal city, the real hometown of actor Brian Cox.
rows.n: Actor Brian Cox pushed for Logan to share his Dundee roots rather than hailing from Quebec.

rows.q: Christmas Eve turns tragic in the pilot of Six Feet Under when Fisher family patriarch Nathaniel is broadsided in his new hearse by this type of transit vehicle.
rows.n: Nathaniel died while lighting a cigarette in his brand-new 2001 Cadillac hearse.

rows.q: Six years before Frasier Crane moved out west, Cheers launched its first, short-lived spin-off in 1987 centered on Carla’s sleazy ex-husband, with this surname.
rows.n: Dan Hedaya starred as Nick Tortelli, who relocated to Las Vegas with his new wife Loretta and his scheming nephew.

rows.q: Following the tragic death of Phil Hartman in 1998, this close friend and former Saturday Night Live castmate joined NewsRadio as newsman Max Louis.
rows.n: Lovitz had previously appeared in the season 4 premiere as an erratic patient threatening to jump off a ledge.

rows.q: Mercenary Jayne Cobb shows rare tenderness on Firefly whenever handling his favorite combat rifle, which he christened with what human feminine name?
rows.n: Jayne tries to trade Vera to Mal in exchange for Saffron in the episode ‘Our Mrs. Reynolds.’

rows.q: In 1994, Norman Lear revisited Archie Bunker’s Queens living room for 704 Hauser, casting this Good Times patriarch as a working-class Black liberal who buys the house.
rows.n: Amos had starred on Good Times, which spun off from Maude, which itself spun off from All in the Family.

rows.q: Created by novelist Colin Dexter, what cantankerous, crossword-loving Oxford police detective was played by John Thaw across 33 television films?
Lost for sixty years, a rare echidna honors David Attenborough, who famously rolled with Rwandan gorillas in what groundbreaking 1979 BBC series?
rows.n: The iconic encounter in Rwanda was impromptu; the gorillas approached Attenborough while cameras rolled.

rows.q: Norman Lear’s Sanford and Son borrowed its premise from the BBC’s Steptoe and Son, moving the junk business from London to this Los Angeles neighborhood.
rows.n: Redd Foxx’s character Fred Sanford was named after his real-life brother.

rows.q: When three weary doctors stop for a drink at Cheers in an episode that birthed the Tommy Westphall crossover universe, they were staff from this fictional Boston hospital.
rows.n: Because St. Elsewhere ended inside a snow globe, the scene theoretically traps dozens of sitcoms in a child’s mind.

rows.q: The Doctor’s TARDIS remains permanently stuck looking like a 1960s British police box thanks to a chronic malfunction in this cloaking mechanism.
rows.n: In the 1963 pilot, Susan notes that the circuit was supposed to change the ship’s exterior to blend in.

rows.q: Walter White cooked for Los Pollos Hermanos, but the fast-food chain was just a subsidiary of this German conglomerate with a dipping-sauce executive.
rows.n: Madrigal executive Peter Schuler met his end with a defibrillator in a company bathroom.

rows.q: In an unusual 2008 writers’ swap, the writing staff of CSI penned an episode of this raunchy Chuck Lorre sitcom, while its writers scripted a Vegas murder mystery.
rows.n: Charlie Sheen and Jon Cryer made brief uncredited cameos on CSI as part of the meta primetime stunt.

rows.q: In season three of The Crown, Princess Margaret sparks a tabloid scandal after being photographed with young gardener Roddy Llewellyn on what private Caribbean island?
Heavily promoted as NBC’s replacement for Friends in 2003, this disastrous American remake of a hit Steven Moffat sitcom was pulled after just four episodes.
rows.n: Moffat loosely based the original UK series on his real-life romance with producer Sue Vertue.

rows.q: Bob Odenkirk directed an unaired 2008 American pilot of this cult Channel 4 sitcom, much to the annoyance of creators Simon Pegg and Jessica Hynes.
rows.n: Creators Pegg and Edgar Wright publicly voiced anger that the US pilot was made without them.

rows.q: In the British House of Cards, Machiavellian whip Francis Urquhart deflects media questions with the phrase: ‘You might very well think that; I couldn’t possibly…’ what?
rows.n: Ian Richardson’s fourth-wall breaks inspired Kevin Spacey’s delivery in the Netflix remake.

rows.q: Before city slickers Oliver and Lisa Douglas moved there in Green Acres, this rural valley community was already the setting for Petticoat Junction.
rows.n: Frank Cady played general store owner Sam Drucker across both shows, occasionally appearing on both the same week.

rows.q: Ferengi business culture is guided by a sacred canon of 285 capitalist aphorisms known collectively by what four-word legalistic title?
rows.n: Rule number one states: ‘Once you have their money, you never give it back.’

rows.q: Three years before landing Joey Tribbiani on Friends, Matt LeBlanc played a dimwitted aspiring model on Top of the Heap, a short-lived spin-off of this Fox sitcom.
rows.n: LeBlanc’s character, Vinnie Verducci, was introduced as an off-and-on love interest for Christina Applegate’s Kelly.

rows.q: George R.R. Martin based the Red Wedding on the 1440 Black Dinner in Scotland, where a young earl was served the severed head of this livestock animal right before his death.
rows.n: In medieval Scottish tradition, presenting a black bull’s head at a banquet signaled doom.

rows.q: Introduced by a virtual white museum and an iconic pan-flute theme, what 1990s PBS nature series was adapted from a line of Dorling Kindersley books?
rows.n: Welsh composer Guy Dagul wrote the memorable pan-flute and synthesizer theme tune.

rows.q: Bill Cosby’s 1996 CBS sitcom Cosby was an official remake of this BBC comedy starring Richard Wilson as the permanently disgruntled retiree Victor Meldrew.
rows.n: Victor Meldrew became famous across Britain for his exasperated catchphrase, ‘I don’t believe it!’

rows.q: After Dorothy remarried, the remaining Golden Girls bought a Miami hotel in The Golden Palace, hiring this future Marvel star and Oscar nominee as their manager.
rows.n: Cheadle played manager Roland Wilson opposite Cheech Marin as the hotel’s energetic chef Chuy Castillos.

rows.q: Both versions of Shameless follow patriarch Frank Gallagher, but the British original was set on the fictional Chatsworth estate in this northern industrial city.
rows.n: Creator Paul Abbott based the Gallagher family dynamic on his own upbringing in Lancashire.

rows.q: Armando Iannucci conquered American politics with Veep, but first introduced this foul-mouthed Downing Street director of communications on BBC’s The Thick of It.
rows.n: Peter Capaldi played the character, loosely based on Tony Blair’s press chief Alastair Campbell.

rows.q: When George Clooney departed ER in 1999, his character Dr. Doug Ross stepped down from County General to take a medical job in this Pacific Northwest city.
rows.n: Julianna Margulies’ character, Carol Hathaway, reunited with Ross there in an unannounced cameo a year later.

rows.q: Suburbia was the perfect disguise in The Americans, where Philip and Elizabeth Jennings hid their KGB identities behind an agency booking this service.
rows.n: The job provided a foolproof excuse for frequent flights, road trips, and odd hours.

rows.q: Agent Dale Cooper happily racks up bills for black coffee and cherry pie at this small-town eatery operated by Norma Jennings.
rows.n: Exterior scenes were filmed at the real Twede’s Cafe in North Bend, Washington.

rows.q: Winston Churchill fumes over an unflattering 80th-birthday portrait in The Crown, leading his wife to burn the canvas created by this real English painter.
rows.n: Sutherland’s preparatory sketches survived, but the final canvas was burned at Chartwell.

rows.q: Louisiana detectives Rust Cohle and Marty Hart crossed paths with the Yellow King on True Detective, borrowing lore from an 1895 book by this American weird-fiction author.
rows.n: Chambers’ book The King in Yellow inspired H.P. Lovecraft before finding new life on HBO.

rows.q: Voice actress Cree Summer voiced the sweet neighbor Susie Carmichael on Rugrats as well as this gadget-wielding tomboy in Inspector Gadget.
rows.n: Summer got the role of Penny in 1983 when she was just fourteen years old.

rows.q: Tom Kenny voices SpongeBob SquarePants and this tragically senile royal villain who kidnaps princesses in Adventure Time.
rows.n: The Ice King’s tragic backstory as Simon Petrikov was revealed in the season 3 episode ‘Holly Jolly Secrets’.

rows.q: CBS executive Fred Silverman got the name for Scooby-Doo from the nonsense scatting Frank Sinatra sang at the end of this 1966 chart-topper.
rows.n: Sinatra improvised “doo-be-doo-be-doo” as the track faded out; Silverman heard it on a red-eye flight.

rows.q: Before turning into the armor-clad Battle Cat with a zap from the Sword of Power, Prince Adam’s cowardly green pet tiger answered to what name?
Trained in the Arashikage ninja clan alongside rival Storm Shadow, what commando dressed in all-black and maintained a strict vow of silence?
rows.n: Hasbro left his action figure unpainted black in 1982 simply to save on manufacturing costs.

rows.q: “I knew I should have stayed home today” was the perpetual catchphrase of this bespectacled ginger student on The Magic School Bus.
rows.n: He famously removed his helmet on Pluto just to prove a point, freezing his head solid.

rows.q: Inspector Gadget’s bumbling voice was provided by Don Adams, who basically recycled his secret agent routine from this 1960s TV spoof.
rows.n: Adams had a 10% ownership stake in the cartoon, making him a fortune in syndication.

rows.q: Calvin and Hobbes invented this chaotic, mask-wearing sport where the score is arbitrary and the only permanent rule is that players can never use the same rule twice.
rows.n: Watterson intended the game as a critique of organized team sports, which he felt crushed childhood creativity.

rows.q: Introduced in 1942, Two-Face initially carried this surname, altered to Dent after three issues to avoid confusing readers with Superman.
rows.n: Bob Kane and Bill Finger renamed Harvey Kent to Harvey Dent to ensure zero overlap with Clark.

rows.q: The voice of Samurai Jack and Justice League’s Green Lantern John Stewart, Phil LaMarr, also voiced this Rastafarian bureaucrat on Futurama.
rows.n: The character was originally named Dexter and lacked a Jamaican accent until LaMarr read for it.

rows.q: In Disney’s 2021 animated hit Encanto, Mirabel struggles with feeling ordinary as the only member of this miraculous Colombian family born without gifts.
rows.n: The family’s enchanted, sentient house is simply called “Casita,” which translates from Spanish as “little house.”

rows.q: Inconsistent ink coverage on cheap newsprint forced Marvel to quickly abandon this original skin color for the Incredible Hulk in 1962.
rows.n: Stan Lee chose green for issue two simply because the printers could apply that hue reliably.

rows.q: When he wasn’t complaining of push-button finger fatigue, George Jetson earned his futuristic paycheck at a company making these toothed parts.
rows.n: Spacely Space Sprockets was locked in an endless rivalry with Spencer Cogswell’s Cogswell Cogs.

rows.q: Shredder’s bumbling henchman Rocksteady is a mutated rhino. His punk-rock partner Bebop is a mutated version of what other animal?
rows.n: They were created specifically for the cartoon so Playmates could sell more action figures.

rows.q: Billed as the “World’s Cutest Kitten,” what small grey cat constantly annoyed Garfield until he threatened to ship him to Abu Dhabi?
rows.n: Despite the eyelashes and high-pitched voice, creator Jim Davis confirmed Nermal is male.

rows.q: Conan O’Brien modeled Lyle Lanley’s show-stopping monorail sales pitch in *The Simpsons* after Harold Hill’s fast-talking patter song “Ya Got Trouble” from which classic 1957 Broadway musical?
rows.n: O’Brien later sang the Monorail song live at the Hollywood Bowl with a backing chorus in 2014.

rows.q: Angelica Pickles rarely went anywhere on Rugrats without this disheveled, balding doll, whose name nods to a synthetic fabric.
rows.n: Cynthia had her own workout song, “Do the Cynthia,” complete with stiff-limbed choreography.

rows.q: Living among saguaro cacti in the California desert near Needles, Snoopy’s skinny, mustachioed brother shares his name with a vampire from Sunnydale.
rows.n: Charles Schulz named Snoopy’s brother after his own childhood dog, who was the real-life model for Snoopy.

rows.q: In a 2003 episode, Cartman starves Butters in a fallout shelter so he can visit this real-life Mexican theme restaurant in Lakewood, Colorado, which Trey Parker and Matt Stone bought in 2021.
rows.n: The creators spent over $40 million refurbishing the cliff-diving landmark before reopening it.

rows.q: Bobby Generic’s overactive imagination and squeaky voice were supplied by this Deal or No Deal host, who also created the Saturday morning show.
rows.n: Mandel developed Bobby’s voice while doing stand-up comedy in the 1970s and ’80s.

rows.q: Even after he signed an exclusive contract with Warner Bros. in 1941, this voice actor’s recorded laugh was reused for decades by Woody Woodpecker.
Fry blows an accrued billionaire fortune at a 31st-century auction just to secure the final existing tin of which extinct pizza topping, wiped out in the 2200s?
After Adam West died in 2017, Quahog High was rechristened in his memory, stripping the name of which real-life, Rhode Island-raised actor who spent years guest-starring as Peter’s nemesis?
rows.n: Woods voiced himself in eight episodes, gleefully playing an eccentric, vengeful supervillain.

rows.q: Bugs Bunny’s battle cry “Of course you realize, this means war!” was lifted word-for-word from this mustachioed comedian in the 1933 film Duck Soup.
rows.n: Bugs also borrowed his signature cigar-like carrot posture and eyebrow waggles from Groucho.

rows.q: Brian Michael Bendis was inspired to create Miles Morales after seeing this actor wear Spider-Man pajamas on the sitcom Community.
rows.n: Glover later voiced Miles in an animated series and made an appearance in Spider-Man: Homecoming.

rows.q: Before a car crash mangled his hands and led him to the Ancient One, Stephen Strange made his fortune in this medical specialty.
rows.n: Strange exhausted his wealth pursuing unproven surgical remedies before traveling to the Himalayas.

rows.q: Developed by Disney’s WED Enterprises for the 1964 New York World’s Fair, what robotic technology brought an artificial Abraham Lincoln to lifelike speech and movement?
rows.n: Audiences were astonished when the synthetic Lincoln stood up from his chair to deliver excerpts from his speeches.

rows.q: Jerry Robinson and Bill Finger modeled the Joker’s unnerving grin on actor Conrad Veidt in this 1928 silent film drama.
rows.n: Veidt played Gwynplaine, a tragic figure whose face was carved into a perpetual smile as a child.

rows.q: Clancy Brown is the voice of SpongeBob’s penny-pinching boss Mr. Krabs, but Marvel fans know his booming tones as this fiery lord of Muspelheim in Thor: Ragnarok.
rows.n: Brown also played the villainous prison guard Captain Hadley in The Shawshank Redemption.

rows.q: Pepé Le Pew’s aggressive romantic pursuits are reliably ignited when this unfortunate black cat accidentally acquires a white painted stripe.
rows.n: Penelope was almost always mute, communicating her frantic escapes entirely through purrs, yowls, and screeches.

rows.q: Wonder Woman didn’t invent the name Diana Prince; in her 1942 comic debut, she bought the identity from an army woman in this profession.
rows.n: The real Diana Prince sold her name and credentials so she could afford to join her fiancé in South America.

rows.q: Years before creating *King of the Hill*, Mike Judge introduced Hank’s obvious spiritual predecessor, a perpetually annoyed World War II veteran with what two-word name?
rows.n: Judge used essentially the same voice and mannerisms when developing Hank Hill for Fox a few years later.

rows.q: Debuting in 1897, this slapstick comic strip about rebellious German-American twins Hans and Fritz is the oldest comic strip still in syndication.
rows.n: The name comes from the German slang for a terrible hangover, literally translating to ‘the cat’s wail.’

rows.q: When Butters terrorizes the town under his villainous mantle Professor Chaos, he recruits a bullied second-grader named Dougie to serve as which military-ranked, punny sidekick?
rows.n: Disarray regularly deflates Chaos’s evil schemes by pointing out that The Simpsons already did it.

rows.q: Beyond alligators and crocodiles, what vascular catastrophe does Sterling Archer repeatedly rank as one of his top three greatest fears, calling it a silent killer that can strike anytime?
rows.n: Archer’s obsession is justified when an aneurysm actually claims an agent in season four.

rows.q: Set in a surreal version of Arizona’s Coconino County, George Herriman’s Krazy Kat famously centers on Ignatz Mouse pelting Krazy with this object.
rows.n: Because Krazy loved Ignatz, the cat happily interpreted every painful head injury as a sign of affection.

rows.q: Created by Alex Raymond in 1934 to rival Buck Rogers, Flash Gordon travels through space to save Earth from Ming the Merciless, the ruler of this planet.
rows.n: George Lucas originally wanted to adapt Flash Gordon, but when denied the rights, he wrote Star Wars instead.

rows.q: Kept hidden for thirteen seasons while he mumbled beside an alley cooler, Boomhauer’s day job was finally revealed in the series finale by a badge showing he worked for which state law agency?
rows.n: The finale also flashed his driver’s license, confirming his first name is Jeffrey.

rows.q: The acclaimed 2018 *BoJack Horseman* episode “Free Churro” is a tour de force consisting of BoJack delivering a bitter, uninterrupted 25-minute monologue at which formal family gathering?
rows.n: BoJack realizes at the very end that he was delivering the speech in the wrong funeral parlor room.

rows.q: Lee Falk’s masked hero The Phantom operates from deep within the Bengali jungle, basing his operations inside a cavern carved to resemble this bone.
rows.n: Inside the cave sits the Skull Throne, where the Phantom listens to tribal oaths and plans justice.

rows.q: On MTV’s *Daria*, slacker heartthrob Trent Lane leads which alt-grunge garage band, whose members constantly announce they are thinking about changing their name?
rows.n: Despite threatening to rebrand in nearly every appearance, the band kept the name for the entire series.

rows.q: Banished from the planet Zetox for inventing a doomsday machine, the floating green alien the Great Gazoo was voiced by which comedic actor, a future star of *The Carol Burnett Show*?
rows.n: Gazoo was an unpopular addition among fans and only appeared in the final season of the original run.

rows.q: Dagwood Bumstead spends his workdays ducking this furious, pint-sized boss, whose surname doubles as an English verb meaning to waver or act indecisively.
rows.n: His tyrannical behavior at the office disappears at home, where he is completely terrified of his wife Cora.

rows.q: Fred Flintstone’s catchphrase “Yabba Dabba Doo!” was an ad-lib inspired by a 1950s commercial jingle for this brand of men’s hair pomade.
rows.n: The original slogan was “A little dab’ll do ya.” Voice actor Alan Reed asked to tweak it during recording.

rows.q: Besides being the definitive voice of the Joker in Batman: The Animated Series, Mark Hamill voiced this fiery, tyrannical Fire Lord in Avatar: The Last Airbender.
rows.n: Hamill went uncredited on several early Avatar episodes to keep Ozai’s face-reveal a surprise.

rows.q: In Hägar the Horrible, the bearded Viking chieftain raids Europe with this dim-witted lieutenant, whose ironic nickname contradicts his misfortune.
Beetle Bailey spends his enlistment goofing off and getting pummeled by Sarge at this fictional, chronically muddy U.S. Army training base.
rows.n: Mort Walker based the base on his own World War II station at Camp Crowder in Missouri.

rows.q: In the Dragon Ball universe, what magical yellow mode of aerial transportation does Master Roshi gift to Goku?
rows.n: In Akira Toriyama’s original Japanese manga, the cloud is known as Kinto’un.

rows.q: Behind the wheel of the rocket-powered Mean Machine, Wacky Races villain Dick Dastardly flew down tracks in a car bearing this numeral.
rows.n: Despite his elaborate sabotage schemes, Dastardly was the only driver in the series to never win a race.

rows.q: Animators at this legendary theatrical studio gave Superman the ability to fly in the 1940s because drawing him leaping looked ridiculous.
rows.n: DC granted special permission for the change, which the comic books soon adopted as standard canon.

rows.q: Marvin the Martian repeatedly attempts to obliterate Earth with an explosive space modulator because it blocks his telescope view of this planet.
rows.n: Chuck Jones created Marvin as a quiet, soft-spoken foil to bombastic Looney Tunes villains like Yosemite Sam.

rows.q: Cartoon flapper Betty Boop was the target of a 1932 lawsuit by this baby-voiced singer, who claimed the character stole her trademark catchphrase.
rows.n: Kane lost when court evidence showed she had swiped “Boop-oop-a-doop” from Black jazz singer Baby Esther.

rows.q: To distance T’Challa from the revolutionary political party sharing his moniker, Marvel briefly rebranded him in 1972 as this big cat.
rows.n: Stan Lee quickly reverted the name after readers complained the change felt pandering and unnatural.

rows.q: In Disney’s Beauty and the Beast, David Ogden Stiers voiced the fussy clock Cogsworth, but he also directed his vocals toward alien experiments as this mad scientist in Lilo & Stitch.
rows.n: Stiers also served as the opening narrator for Beauty and the Beast.

rows.q: Known for his rogue’s gallery of bizarre villains, Dick Tracy spent a famous 1944 storyline pursuing this freelance hitman with an aerodynamically level skull.
rows.n: Chester Gould reportedly received grieving fan letters and funeral wreaths when Flattop was killed off.

rows.q: Walt Disney took a huge gamble by scrapping and remaking this 1932 Silly Symphony in three-strip Technicolor, winning animation’s first Oscar.
Hanna-Barbera’s Jonny Quest relied for protection not on police, but on this white-haired government agent who acted as his bodyguard.
rows.n: Animator Doug Wildey based Bannon’s rugged, lantern-jawed design on comic strip icon Steve Canyon.

rows.q: Before mysteriously vanishing from the comic in 1983, this mustachioed roommate of Jon Arbuckle was the original owner of Odie.
rows.n: Jim Davis phased Lyman out once he realized Garfield and Jon could communicate directly without a third wheel.

rows.q: Tara Strong voices Harley Quinn and Fairly OddParents’ Timmy Turner, as well as this bookish, lilac-colored unicorn who leads My Little Pony: Friendship Is Magic.
rows.n: Strong only did the speaking voice; Rebecca Shoichet handled Twilight’s singing parts.

rows.q: Speed runs in the family, but not always: Speedy Gonzales has a famously lethargic, gun-toting cousin known by this sluggish name.
When Tom and Jerry debuted in 1940’s Puss Gets the Boot, the famous animated cat answered to this down-home, six-letter moniker.
rows.n: The mouse was unnamed on screen in that short, though the animation crew privately called him Jinx.

rows.q: Striking this ordinary mobility aid against the ground is how mild-mannered physician Donald Blake transformed into the Mighty Thor.
rows.n: The cane disguised Mjolnir; striking it also turned Blake back into his mortal persona.

rows.q: In his 1938 debut, Clark Kent didn’t work for the Daily Planet, typing his earliest scoops for a newspaper with this celestial name.
rows.n: Joe Shuster named the paper after the Toronto Daily Star, where he had worked as a newsboy in his youth.

rows.q: Gotham’s cryogenically obsessed villain Mr. Freeze debuted in 1959 under this numerical moniker before the 1960s TV series renamed him.
rows.n: The television show adopted Mr. Freeze for actor George Sanders, and DC made the swap permanent.

rows.q: Alan Moore originally planned to use Charlton Comics heroes for Watchmen, basing the godlike Doctor Manhattan on this nuclear-powered soldier.
rows.n: DC made Moore invent original characters so the Charlton acquisition could remain in the main continuity.

rows.q: Before settling on the stone-age pun that ran for six seasons on ABC, Hanna-Barbera produced an unsold 1959 pilot under what slightly less prehistoric surname?
rows.n: Voice acting veteran Daws Butler originally provided Fred’s voice before Alan Reed took over the role.

rows.q: Turanga Leela’s distinctive first name was lifted straight from a sprawling 1948 ten-movement orchestral symphony composed by which French avant-garde master?
rows.n: Messiaen’s Turangalila-Symphonie famously featured the ondes Martenot, an eerie electronic instrument.

rows.q: In a 1950 Chuck Jones cartoon, Daffy Duck pitches an action script to a Warner Bros. boss, starring himself as what swashbuckling, bread-punned hero?
rows.n: The short parodied Baroness Orczy’s 1905 adventure novel The Scarlet Pimpernel.

rows.q: In 1967, Bob Dylan and The Band retreated to a pink rental house in West Saugerties to record the Basement Tapes, just outside what namesake Hudson Valley arts colony?
rows.n: The historic 1969 festival borrowed the town’s name despite taking place 40 miles away.

rows.q: A Californian roommate suggested what name for Tom Johnston and Patrick Simmons’ mellow rock group, poking fun at their habit of smoking joints?
